newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: INVESTMENTS TO PUSH CLT-UFA INTO LOSS -AUDIOFINA.
newsitem.headline: INVESTMENTS TO PUSH CLT-UFA INTO LOSS -AUDIOFINA.

text.p: Profitability at Luxembourg- German radio and television group CLT-UFA will suffer in 1997 as a result of investment in countries including Great Britain, France and Poland, holding company Audiofina , which controls CLT-UFA, said on Thursday.
"Pre-tax results will be close to break-even in 1997 and the group result after tax will be between minus 1.5 billion and minus 2.0 billion francs," Audiofina said in a statement.

The investments would weigh on results in the short term before creating value for shareholders. In the medium term the new developments by CLT-UFA and "traditional" sources of income would generate some 5.0 billion francs in profits.

For Audiofina, which consolidates 50 percent of CLT-UFA's results, this would mean a loss of one billion francs in 1997. But at Audiofina 1997 would also be marked by a book gain of 21.5 billion as a result of the merger between CLT and UFA.

Audiofina said it expected to receive one billion francs in dividends from its 3.3 percent holding in France's Havas and cash management. In total 1997 group profit should be between 21 billion and 22 billion francs.

Audiofina said that in view of its confidence in the developments undertaken by CLT-UFA it had asked CLT-UFA not to change its dividend policy despite the 1997 loss. Audiofina itself would continue to increase dividends.
Audiofina paid 22 francs per share in 1996.
CLT-UFA, 50-50 owned by Audiofina and German media and publishing group Bertelsmann , is planning investments in Britain's Channel-5, TPS in France and RTL7 in Poland.
CLT-UFA, merged in January, had 1996 consolidated net profit of 3.37 billion francs, up from 3.34 billion in 1995.
Audiofina consolidated net profit rose by two percent in 1996 to 3.23 billion francs.
